text: On 24 February 2014 the applicants participated in a spontaneous gathering in front of the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow.

The applicants came to the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow to attend a public hearing involving activists who were on trial in relation to mass disorders at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow on 6 May 2012.
The applicants were arrested during the gathering in front of the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow on 24 February 2014.
The applicants were convicted of administrative offences following their arrest during the gathering on 24 February 2014.
The applicants' details are set out in the appended table.
The applicant in application no. 47800/14 was represented before the Court by Mr A. Savelyev, a lawyer practising in Domodedovo.
The applicants in application no. 67936/14 were represented before the Court by the lawyers of the Memorial Human Rights Centre and the European Human Rights Advocacy Centre (EHRAC).
The applicant in application no. 68196/14 was represented before the Court by Mr N. Zboroshenko, a lawyer practising in Moscow.
The Russian Government were initially represented before the Court by Mr G. Matyushkin, Representative of the Russian Federation to the European Court of Human Rights.

The Russian Government were subsequently represented before the Court by Mr M. Galperin, who succeeded Mr G. Matyushkin as Representative of the Russian Federation to the European Court of Human Rights.
The facts of the case, as submitted by the parties, may be summarised as follows.
On the morning of 24 February 2014 the applicants were among some 150 people who came to the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow.

The applicants came to the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow to attend the public delivery of the judgment in the criminal case concerning mass disorders at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow on 6 May 2012.
The court-house of the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow was cordoned off by the police on the morning of 24 February 2014.
The applicants could not enter the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow because it was cordoned off by the police.
The applicants remained outside the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow among other members of the public who were also aspiring to attend the hearing, thus forming a gathering.

Further details about the gathering outside the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow on 24 February 2014 are described in Navalnyy v. Russia [GC], nos. 29580/12 and 4 others, §§ 35-42, 15 November 2018.
At different times the applicants were arrested and transferred to a police station following the gathering outside the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow on 24 February 2014.
Details regarding the administrative proceedings against each applicant are outlined in the Appendix.

Article 20.2 § 5 of the Code of Administrative Offences provides that violation by a participant in a public event of the established procedure for conducting a public event is punishable with a fine of 10,000 to 20,000 roubles.

Article 20.2 § 5 of the Code of Administrative Offences provides that violation by a participant in a public event of the established procedure for conducting a public event is punishable with up to forty hours of community work.
A summary of other relevant domestic provisions is set out in Navalnyy v. Russia [GC], nos. 29580/12 and 4 others, §§ 46-47, 15 November 2018.
A summary of other relevant domestic provisions is set out in Lashmankin and Others v. Russia, nos. 57818/09 and 14 others, §§ 223 and 226, 7 February 2017.
A summary of other relevant domestic provisions is set out in Korneyeva v. Russia, no. 72051/17, §§ 22-26, 8 October 2019.
The domestic legal provisions governing administrative transfer (escorting) and detention are set out in Butkevich v. Russia, no. 5865/07, §§ 33-36, 13 February 2018.

According to Article 31.9 of the Code of Administrative Offences, if a decision imposing an administrative punishment is not enforced during two years from its entry into force, it can no longer be executed.

According to Article 31.9 of the Code of Administrative Offences, the time when enforcement of a decision imposing an administrative punishment is suspended or stayed is excluded from the two-year period after which the decision can no longer be executed.
